blocks.content: This topic gets precise about exactly where desired state and current state actually live, both on the very same object, in two distinct subresources, a real API detail worth understanding precisely.
1. Two Fields, Both Stored in etcd
blocks.text: 1. Two Fields, Both Stored in etcd

blocks.content: Every object's .spec field holds its desired state, and its .status field holds its current, observed state, exactly the fields referenced casually throughout this course, both are genuinely stored in etcd, covered in its own topic later in this module.

blocks.alt: Two distinct fields, both genuinely persisted, on the exact same object

blocks.content: 2. Status Is Updated by Continuous Observation
blocks.text: 2. Status Is Updated by Continuous Observation

blocks.content: Unlike .spec, which you (or a higher-level controller) set deliberately, .status is continuously updated by whatever component is actually observing reality, kubelet reporting a Pod's real state, for instance, it reflects what genuinely is, not what was declared.

blocks.alt: Continuously updated by observation, reflecting reality, not a declared intention

blocks.content: 3. The Same Object, Two Real Subresources
blocks.text: 3. The Same Object, Two Real Subresources

blocks.content: This is a genuine API detail worth knowing: spec and status are not just conceptually different, they are actually distinct subresources of the same object in the Kubernetes API, each independently addressable.

blocks.alt: Genuinely distinct, independently addressable subresources of one single object

blocks.content:
kubectl get pod my-app -o jsonpath='{.spec}'
kubectl get pod my-app -o jsonpath='{.status}'

code.content:
kubectl get pod my-app -o jsonpath='{.spec}'
kubectl get pod my-app -o jsonpath='{.status}'

codes.bash:
kubectl get pod my-app -o jsonpath='{.spec}'
kubectl get pod my-app -o jsonpath='{.status}'

blocks.content: Because status is its own subresource, RBAC rules (covered in the Security module) can grant permission to update it separately from spec, this is precisely how a controller is permitted to report a Pod's status without also needing broad permission to change what that Pod is supposed to be running.

blocks.alt: Separate, independently grantable permissions for reporting status versus changing intent

blocks.content: 5. The Gap Is the Entire Point
blocks.text: 5. The Gap Is the Entire Point

blocks.content: Every controller covered throughout this course exists, fundamentally, to continuously close the gap between these two fields, spec is the goal, status is reality, and reconciliation, covered in the previous topic, is the ongoing work of bringing the two into alignment.

blocks.alt: The gap between these two fields is, quite literally, every controller's entire reason for existing

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Desired state (.spec) and current state (.status) are genuinely distinct, independently addressable subresources of the exact same object, both stored in etcd.
Every controller's entire purpose is continuously closing the gap between these two fields, spec is the goal, status is the continuously observed reality.
